How to evaluate a trading strategy and when it can fail

Before considering returns, understand when a strategy enters, exits and may fail.

Research guide4 min readPublished by Surfer Quant
01

Start with the return drivers

Trend, range, spread and portfolio strategies rely on different return drivers. A useful description explains triggers, holding periods and exits, connecting performance with market conditions.

02

Put the version back into the record

When instruments, parameters, scaling or execution change, results should remain tied to the relevant version. An unchanged product name does not mean years of results came from one method.

03

Understand possible failure conditions

Useful documentation includes adverse conditions such as false breakouts, persistent one-way markets, correlation shifts and rising costs. Pause criteria and exception handling are part of the research.

This is a general guide to strategy evaluation and operations, not individualized investment advice.
